title: ZephyrSearch - Hosted API embeddings + rerank demo
summary: Introductory hosted API demo focused on embeddings + reranking for improving search relevance. Covered the embeddings endpoint, rerank endpoint, console walkthrough, and Optimize suggestions. Discussed latency vs cost tradeoffs and security requirements (SOC 2, SSO, KMS). Agreed next steps: share pricing, security pack, demo recording, and run a short benchmark/POC with a 2-week pilot.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-21 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Nina Lopez (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (ZephyrSearch PM), Diego Ruiz (ZephyrSearch Eng Lead), Maya Singh (ZephyrSearch DS)

Summary (auto): quick demo of hosted embeddings + rerank, product fit questions, security check, next steps recapped.

00:00 Samir Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Samir from Redwood Inference, I'll run the demo with Nina. How's everyone doing?
00:09 Aisha Khan: Good, thanks. Excited to see how this can help our search relevance problem.
00:13 Nina Lopez: Awesome, quick agenda — we'll do a short overview, show the embeddings endpoint, then rerank, then Console and Optimize tips, and finish w/ Q&A and next steps.
00:29 Diego Ruiz: Sounds good, Diego here, quick context — we're running an Elastic + custom ranking right now, want to add semantic layer, main pain points are long tail queries and latency spikes during peak.
00:41 Nina Lopez: Great, that matches a lot of customers. One thing we'll highlight is how hosted embeddings + rerank can sit in front of your current ES pipeline, so you can keep existing infra and add semantic reranking.
00:58 Maya Singh: Quick question, what's the usual latency for embeddings+rerank? We care about median P95 under 300ms ideally.
01:08 Samir Patel: For hosted, depends on model and batch size — with our curated small embedding model you can expect single-request embeddings around 20-50ms and rerank about 30-120ms, P95 varies; we have performance profiles in the Console. For strict P95 SLOs we sometimes recommend Dedicated, but many customers hit target with hosted plus caching.
01:34 Nina Lopez: I'll demo how caching and prefix/K-V cache — excuse me, KV cache — and batching in Optimize help reduce token cost and tail latency.
01:47 Aisha Khan: Are there any tradeoffs for accuracy when using smaller embedding models or quantized variants?
01:53 Nina Lopez: Yes slight tradeoffs; Optimize will show quality vs cost recommendations. We also support quick A/B tests in Console so you can measure relevance delta on your eval set before rollout.
02:10 Samir Patel: Ok jumping into the Console — share screen (audio omitted).
02:20 Nina Lopez: On the left is Model Catalog, we curate open models and show throughput/latency profiles. I'll call the embeddings endpoint live with a sample doc set.
02:35 Sample API call (spoken): "POST /v1/embeddings with model=redwood-embed-compact and payload..."
02:44 Maya Singh: Can we host our own embeddings? We want to keep vectors in our region for residency.
02:49 Samir Patel: For that we offer Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) — for hosted we have region options and data retention controls. If you need air-gapped, Private is the option.
03:05 Nina Lopez: Running embedding request... results come back, you can see vector size and confidence. Results show top-n nearest neighbors if you plug into the search flow.
03:20 Diego Ruiz: Our corpus has a lot of short product Q&A. How do you recommend indexing? One vector per doc? chunking?
03:27 Nina Lopez: Usually chunk by semantic boundaries — we recommend overlap 20-30 tokens, and use passage-level vectors for recall, then rerank full doc text for precision.
03:40 Samir Patel: Now rerank demo: we send top-k from Elastic, call Redwood rerank endpoint with query + candidates, it returns a score and normalized ordering.
03:55 Nina Lopez: Showing a live rerank call: "POST /v1/rerank model=redwood-rank-mlr payload..." (note: transcript may mis-hear model ids).
04:08 Aisha Khan: How intensive is rerank compute? If we send top-100 for each query is that expensive?
04:15 Samir Patel: It's linear with candidates; top-100 is heavier — Optimize suggests reducing candidate pool via a fast ANN (we integrate with common vector stores) and then rerank top-10-20. You can also use a lightweight ranking model for initial triage.
04:33 Diego Ruiz: Got it. Any batching options for rerank? Like do you support multi-query batching?
04:39 Nina Lopez: Yes, our runtime supports request batching and grouping; Optimize will recommend batch sizes based on your QPS and latency SLO. There's also adaptive batching to preserve tail latency.
04:54 Maya Singh: On metrics side, what observability do we get?
05:00 Samir Patel: Console has per-route latency breakdowns, token-level cost, request traces, and a rollout dashboard for A/B tests. We also export metrics to Prometheus and logs to your SIEM.
05:18 Aisha Khan: Security — we need SOC2, SSO, KMS integration, and audit logs for compliance.
05:24 Nina Lopez: We are SOC 2 compliant, support SAML/SSO, RBAC, and integrate with customer KMS/HSM in Private. For hosted we offer envelope encryption and audit logs; we'll share the security pack.
05:40 Diego Ruiz: Does hosted keep data to serve models? We can't have customer PII used for model training.
05:46 Samir Patel: Hosted by default does not use customer data for model training; we have clear data handling policies and can sign contractual clauses. Private deployments give more control if needed.
05:58 Nina Lopez: Back to performance: here's Optimize's suggestion — it recommends an embedding model + rerank combo and quantization profile; it estimates cost improvement ~35% with minimal delta in hit rate on your seed eval.
06:15 Maya Singh: That estimate assumes X QPS and average doc token length Y, right?
06:20 Nina Lopez: Yes it's workload-aware; you can upload sample requests to get tailored recommendations.
06:28 Aisha Khan: What's the typical integration path? How long to POC?
06:33 Samir Patel: Most teams do a 2-week pilot: you provide a sample corpus and metrics, we run pilot in hosted with scoping for traffic patterns, and share a report. For larger/regulatory customers we do Dedicated or Private with longer lead time.
06:49 Diego Ruiz: Ok good. Cost modelling — do you charge per-token for rerank?
06:54 Samir Patel: Rerank and generation are token-based; embeddings are priced per-embedding unit. For pilots we often give credits to get initial results.
07:05 Maya Singh: Any limits on batch size for embeddings?
07:10 Nina Lopez: We have soft limits to protect latency; Optimize will recommend the sweet spot.
07:16 (sound of typing)
07:22 Aisha Khan: Can we run a small benchmark against our current ES + BM25 + custom features? We'd like side-by-side relevance metrics: MRR, NDCG, latency.
07:31 Samir Patel: Absolutely — that's a good next step. If you can send sample queries and labels we'll run a head-to-head. Diego, you'll provide that?
07:38 Diego Ruiz: Yep I can pull a 2k query set and current metrics.
07:42 Samir Patel: Great — we'll scope a 2-week pilot and estimate cost.
07:49 Nina Lopez: Quick note on fallbacks — some customers use a multi-tier policy: cheap host model for tail and bigger model for core, plus automatic fallback to cheaper variants under load.
08:05 Maya Singh: Any mention of OpenAI compatibility or tooling?
08:09 Samir Patel: We support common API patterns and libraries; many customers switch models without changing top-level app logic.
08:15 (small cross talk)
08:22 Aisha Khan: Questions around data residency — can we guarantee region?
08:26 Nina Lopez: For hosted we have region options; for strict residency, Private is recommended. We'll detail region availability in the security pack.
08:35 Diego Ruiz: Performance deep dive: can we get per-token cost breakdown?
08:40 Samir Patel: Console shows token-level cost for each request and you can drill into model-level spend. Optimize also suggests quantization profiles that reduce unit cost for minimal quality loss.
08:55 Nina Lopez: I'll demo an A/B rollout in Console quickly — create experiment, upload eval set, run rerank configs, view NDCG and hit rate differences.
09:10 Nina Lopez: Here you can see the eval from a past customer: baseline vs rerank improves MRR by ~18% on long-tail queries.
09:24 Aisha Khan: That's promising. Any gotchas for shopping-style queries? We have products with price-sensitive filters.
09:31 Samir Patel: For shopping we recommend hybrid signals: score from rerank + business rules (stock, price). Rerank can be used as a relevance layer then composite score ranks results.
09:45 Maya Singh: Regarding vector stores — do you host vectors or integrate with our existing vector DB?
09:50 Nina Lopez: We integrate with major vector stores, and you can also push vectors to Redwood's managed vector store in hosted if you prefer. For regulated customers many keep vectors in their own store and call Redwood for rerank.
10:05 Diego Ruiz: Ok, timeline and next steps?
10:09 Samir Patel: Recap: we do a 2-week pilot in hosted, ZephyrSearch provides 2k query corpus and labels, Redwood shares pricing and security docs, schedule kickoff meeting and benchmark run.
10:21 Aisha Khan: Who should I expect communications from?
10:25 Samir Patel: I'll send the scoping doc and pricing, Nina will send the security pack.
10:30 Maya Singh: One last question: can rerank be done in streaming mode? We need partial results fast for UX.
10:36 Nina Lopez: Rerank is typically synchronous, but you can stream generation endpoints. For fast UX we recommend precomputing vectors + async rerank updates for personalization. We'll include patterns in the scoping doc.
10:50 Diego Ruiz: Thanks team, this was helpful.
10:54 Samir Patel: Thanks all — we'll follow up with materials and next steps.
11:00 (call ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hear of model names (redwood-embed-compact might be transcribed differently), some technical terms spelled phonetically.
